288:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289:- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
297:- Switch Account (v300.0, replaces the v158.0 `__claudeSuppressTrim`-in-place flow): the account menu lives in the chat page's sidebar, behind the settings dialog, so un-trimming the usage view no longer exposed it. `BeginSwitchAccountAsync` records the account signature (`ReadAccountSignatureAsync` = `sessionKey|lastActiveOrg` cookies, null when signed out), enters `_switchAccountMode`, navigates to `SwitchAccountUrl` (`/new`) and `TryOpenAccountMenu` (from `OnNavigationCompleted`) clicks `[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` (with fallbacks, 40×200 ms poll). While the mode is on, `TryRedirectToUsage` leaves `/new` alone unless the page was signed out (`_sawSignedOutPage`), and `Reload()` does nothing while the tab is on screen — the background refresh must not yank the user out of the menu. `_switchAccountTimer` (2 s, `OnSwitchAccountTimerTick`, busy-guarded) returns to the usage view when the signature differs from the baseline (organization or account switch without a sign-out), ends the mode when the page is back on the usage view or the core is gone, waits on auth paths, and gives up after `SwitchAccountTimeout` (10 min). Refresh, Sign Out and the off-screen `Reload()` end the mode.
299:- Native-mode composer usage button (v235.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatTranscriptView.xaml` `ComposerUsageButton`/`UsagePopup`): a ring after the composer's Permissions selector, shown only for Claude providers. The popup has two halves: the context window of the chat's last completed turn (`ClaudeStatusLineInput` captured in `CompleteNativeTurn`/`CompleteNativeTurnForSession` into `_mainStatusLine` or `NativeChatSessionState.LastStatusLine`, cleared by Clear Chat), and the plan limits read from the cached `LastUsageJson` (the same numbers as the inline bars, so `NoWeeklyLimit`/`HasExtraUsage` are honored). The ring fills with context %, or with the session limit before any turn has reported a window. `HandleScrapedSnapshot` calls `RefreshChatUsageIndicators()`, so an open popup updates in place. Opening the popup raises `UsageRequested`, handled by `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync`: the same account-switch guard the background timer uses first, then `Reload()` when the tab is visible, otherwise `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:false, updateWindowState:false, activate:false)`, so the tab never appears from a ring click. "See detailed breakdown" (`UsageDetailsRequested`) calls `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:true)`, the same as the inline bars. The popup's "Updated / Not updated since" line uses `IsUsageSnapshotStale`. Formatting and ring geometry are pure (`ChatUsageIndicator`, unit-tested in `Tests/ChatUsageIndicatorTests.cs`). Popup rows (v236.0): label column `Auto`, value column `*` right-aligned with `CharacterEllipsis`; the border is `MinWidth=280`/`MaxWidth=440` instead of a fixed 280, because a long value ("0% used · Starts with your first message") in the old `*`/`Auto` layout squeezed the label column and drew over "Current session". `UsageNoPlanText` keeps `MaxWidth=256` so its wrapping does not stretch the popup. "Refreshing…" (v236.0): a ring click sets the view's `_usageRefreshing`, so the last line reads "Refreshing…" (snapshot pushes in the meantime only update the stored `_usageUpdatedText`) until the control calls `EndUsageRefresh()` on the clicked transcript when `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync` finishes. That task waits for real data: the off-screen path through `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync`'s own wait, the visible-tab `Reload()` path on `_indicatorScrapeTcs` (completed in `HandleScrapedSnapshot`, 15 s cap). A click while one is running joins the running `_indicatorRefresh` instead of starting another. Not F5-verified. The popup's wait is capped at `UsageRefreshTextCapMs` (20 s, v268.0): the off-screen path can chain a 10 s silent reload, a WebView2 rebuild (up to 30 s) and another 10 s wait, so "Refreshing…" could sit there over a minute after a fresh sign-in; the refresh itself keeps running and a later snapshot still updates the popup in place. Refresh ring (v276.0): the last line no longer swaps to "Refreshing…" (which hid the time); `UsageUpdatedRow` keeps the "Updated" text and shows `UsageRefreshSpinner` (10 px ring, tooltip "Refreshing…") beside it while `_usageRefreshing`. The rotation is started/stopped with `BeginAnimation` in `ShowUsageUpdatedText` only when the state flips, never by a style trigger (the v265.0 crash). Account line (v300.0): the injected script fetches same-origin `/api/account` once per page load and puts its `email_address` into `UsageSnapshot.AccountEmail`; `BuildChatUsageIndicatorData` passes it on and `UsageAccountText` at the bottom of the popup shows "Account: {0}" (collapsed when empty, e.g. a snapshot cached by an older version). `RefreshLanguage` redoes it.

lines: - Follow-up — the `keep` rule was the same bug (v73.0): the ancestor-side fix alone didn't restore scrolling, because `findIsolationTarget()` can resolve to a `tabindex=-1` dialog shell (not just the small `div.pb-8` block) when the page has one — that shell itself commonly uses `display:flex; flex-direction:column` to stack a header above the internally-scrolling body. The `[data-claude-usage-keep="1"]` rule was still forcing `display:block !important` on the target, which collapses that flex-column and strips the scrollable child's bounded height (its `flex-1`/`min-h-0` become no-ops once the parent isn't a flex container) — the shell's own untouched `overflow:hidden` then just clips the excess with no scrollbar, no matter what the ancestor-side fix does. `keep` now only widens the target (`width`/`max-width`/`margin`/`box-sizing`) and leaves `display`/`height`/`overflow`/`padding` completely alone, same principle as the `scrollbox` rule.

- Docked tab painting over its neighbour (v230.0): the WebView2 is a native child window, so WPF clipping and z-order never apply to it. Measured on a tab docked in the document well with the Output pane below: the control's bottom edge landed at the bottom of the Output pane, i.e. it was laid out ~280 px taller than the area the shell shows, so the shell clipped the WPF elements (status bar) while the native window kept painting over Output. `ClaudeUsageControl`'s guard (`#region WebView2 bounds guard`) runs 150 ms after `SizeChanged`/`IsVisibleChanged`/the frame's `OnSize`, and on a 2 s heartbeat while the control is loaded. (1) `ClampWebViewToVisibleArea` hit-tests the `WebArea` grid (it has a `Transparent` background on purpose — WPF hit testing skips an element with no brush) down its middle: WPF hit testing honors the shell's clip, so the first point that no longer hits one of this control's own visuals is where the pane ends (one hit test when nothing is cut off, a ~7-step binary search otherwise). The web view host then gets an explicit `Height` of the visible part with `VerticalAlignment=Top` (not `MaxHeight`: a non-stretched host sizes to its content and an `HwndHost` desires 0); the clamp is released when the area is fully visible again. (2) `RepairWebViewBounds` compares `GetWindowRect(WebView.Handle)` with where WPF put the element (`PointToScreen` + `ActualWidth/Height` × the DPI transform) through the pure `HostedWindowBounds.IsMisaligned` (2 px tolerance, an element with no area never counts); a mismatch must be seen on two consecutive checks before anything is done, then `NudgeWebViewLayout` (width −1 px and back), and if the window is still wrong `SnapWindowTo` (`SetWindowPos`). Three failed repairs in a row back it off for 60 s. The off-screen scraper is skipped. Diagnostics: every change of state is appended to `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\usage-layout.log` (control/area size, visible height, the frame's own `GetFramePos`, and — only while clipped — the ancestor chain with each element's vertical extent and clip flags; restarted past 200 KB). If the overlap ever returns, that file says whether WPF's layout, the shell's clip or the window itself is the one that is off.

- Settings-as-dialog route (v300.0): claude.ai now redirects `/settings/usage` to `/new#settings/usage` and draws settings as a fixed `role=dialog` (`cds-dialog-regions`, a grid capped at `max-height:800px`) over the chat page. Every check that compared the *path* with `/settings/usage` failed there, so `TryRedirectToUsage` took `/new` for a post-auth landing and navigated back to the usage URL every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s throttle) — the "keeps refreshing" report — and `TryRestoreTrim`/Refresh misjudged the page too. `ClaudeUsagePage.IsUsagePage(Uri)` (pure, `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs`, unit-tested) accepts either the path or the `#settings/usage` fragment and is used everywhere the C# side asks "is this the usage view"; `ClaudeUsagePage.IsAuthPath` holds the `/login`/`/logout`/`/magic-link`/`/auth` prefixes. The injected script has its own `isUsagePage()` (pathname or hash): it trims and posts snapshots only there, so a `/new` page is never trimmed or scraped. Layout: the trim CSS stretches the kept dialog to the whole viewport (`position:fixed; inset:0; max-height:none; border-radius:0; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`) and hides its title row (`.col-span-full.row-start-1`, which holds claude.ai's X — closing it would leave the bare chat page); the dialog's own `overflow-y-auto` pane keeps scrolling to the end. Verified live in Edge with the extension's cookies at 1142×616.

-- Switch Account (v300.0, replaces the v158.0 `__claudeSuppressTrim`-in-place flow): the account menu lives in the chat page's sidebar, behind the settings dialog, so un-trimming the usage view no longer exposed it. `BeginSwitchAccountAsync` records the account signature (`ReadAccountSignatureAsync` = `sessionKey|lastActiveOrg` cookies, null when signed out), enters `_switchAccountMode`, navigates to `SwitchAccountUrl` (`/new`) and `TryOpenAccountMenu` (from `OnNavigationCompleted`) clicks `[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` (with fallbacks, 40×200 ms poll). While the mode is on, `TryRedirectToUsage` leaves `/new` alone unless the page was signed out (`_sawSignedOutPage`), and `Reload()` does nothing while the tab is on screen — the background refresh must not yank the user out of the menu. `_switchAccountTimer` (2 s, `OnSwitchAccountTimerTick`, busy-guarded) returns to the usage view when the signature differs from the baseline (organization or account switch without a sign-out), ends the mode when the page is back on the usage view or the core is gone, waits on auth paths, and gives up after `SwitchAccountTimeout` (10 min). Refresh, Sign Out and the off-screen `Reload()` end the mode.

+- Switch Account (v301.0, replaces the v300.0 account-menu flow): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` deletes the shared cookie copy (`SharedCookiePath`, which would sign a rebuilt view back in as the same account), resets `_lastCookieSaveUtc` and navigates to `LogoutUrl` (`https://claude.ai/logout`, the `href` of claude.ai's own "Log out" menu item). `/logout` is an auth path, so `_sawSignedOutPage` is set and `TryRedirectToUsage` brings the usage view back after the next sign-in. Unlike Sign out (`SignOutAsync`, which clears all site data), the Google session stays, so Google sign-in offers the accounts it knows. With no live core it falls back to `SignOutAsync`. Why the v300.0 flow was dropped: it opened claude.ai's account menu (`[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` on `/new`) and the user's "add account" path from there is claude.ai's add/switch-account login, which locks the e-mail and disables "Continue with Google" (`disabled` when that flow is active). The switch-mode state (`_switchAccountMode`, timer, cookie signature poll, `Reload()`/redirect exceptions) went with it.

-- Native-mode composer usage button (v235.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatTranscriptView.xaml` `ComposerUsageButton`/`UsagePopup`): a ring after the composer's Permissions selector, shown only for Claude providers. The popup has two halves: the context window of the chat's last completed turn (`ClaudeStatusLineInput` captured in `CompleteNativeTurn`/`CompleteNativeTurnForSession` into `_mainStatusLine` or `NativeChatSessionState.LastStatusLine`, cleared by Clear Chat), and the plan limits read from the cached `LastUsageJson` (the same numbers as the inline bars, so `NoWeeklyLimit`/`HasExtraUsage` are honored). The ring fills with context %, or with the session limit before any turn has reported a window. `HandleScrapedSnapshot` calls `RefreshChatUsageIndicators()`, so an open popup updates in place. Opening the popup raises `UsageRequested`, handled by `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync`: the same account-switch guard the background timer uses first, then `Reload()` when the tab is visible, otherwise `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:false, updateWindowState:false, activate:false)`, so the tab never appears from a ring click. "See detailed breakdown" (`UsageDetailsRequested`) calls `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:true)`, the same as the inline bars. The popup's "Updated / Not updated since" line uses `IsUsageSnapshotStale`. Formatting and ring geometry are pure (`ChatUsageIndicator`, unit-tested in `Tests/ChatUsageIndicatorTests.cs`). Popup rows (v236.0): label column `Auto`, value column `*` right-aligned with `CharacterEllipsis`; the border is `MinWidth=280`/`MaxWidth=440` instead of a fixed 280, because a long value ("0% used · Starts with your first message") in the old `*`/`Auto` layout squeezed the label column and drew over "Current session". `UsageNoPlanText` keeps `MaxWidth=256` so its wrapping does not stretch the popup. "Refreshing…" (v236.0): a ring click sets the view's `_usageRefreshing`, so the last line reads "Refreshing…" (snapshot pushes in the meantime only update the stored `_usageUpdatedText`) until the control calls `EndUsageRefresh()` on the clicked transcript when `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync` finishes. That task waits for real data: the off-screen path through `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync`'s own wait, the visible-tab `Reload()` path on `_indicatorScrapeTcs` (completed in `HandleScrapedSnapshot`, 15 s cap). A click while one is running joins the running `_indicatorRefresh` instead of starting another. Not F5-verified. The popup's wait is capped at `UsageRefreshTextCapMs` (20 s, v268.0): the off-screen path can chain a 10 s silent reload, a WebView2 rebuild (up to 30 s) and another 10 s wait, so "Refreshing…" could sit there over a minute after a fresh sign-in; the refresh itself keeps running and a later snapshot still updates the popup in place. Refresh ring (v276.0): the last line no longer swaps to "Refreshing…" (which hid the time); `UsageUpdatedRow` keeps the "Updated" text and shows `UsageRefreshSpinner` (10 px ring, tooltip "Refreshing…") beside it while `_usageRefreshing`. The rotation is started/stopped with `BeginAnimation` in `ShowUsageUpdatedText` only when the state flips, never by a style trigger (the v265.0 crash). Fiz as três coisas. Compila e os 1085 testes unitários passam, mas nada disso foi testado dentro do VS ainda.

**1. Botão do Google.** Não mudei código nenhum para ele. Ele já funcionou na instância Exp que você testou, e acho que descobri o motivo de ficar cinza. O "Trocar conta" antigo abria o menu de conta do claude.ai, e o caminho "adicionar conta" de lá abre um login que trava o e-mail. Nesse modo o próprio claude.ai desativa o "Continuar com o Google". Com a mudança do item 2, o "Trocar conta" não passa mais por esse caminho.

**2. "Trocar conta" agora clica no "Sair".** O botão abre o mesmo link do "Sair" do claude.ai (`/logout`) e cai na tela de login. Depois que você entra com outra conta, o painel volta sozinho para a tela de uso.
- A sessão do Google é mantida, então ele já oferece as contas que conhece.
- O botão "Sign out" continua apagando tudo, inclusive a sessão do Google.
- O código antigo do menu de conta foi removido, e o tooltip do botão foi atualizado e traduzido nos 19 idiomas.

**3. Conta no popup de uso.** O "Conta:" agora mostra o e-mail com que o próprio Claude Code (a CLI) está logado, lido do `.claude.json` e separado entre Windows e WSL. O e-mail da conta do Claude Usage não aparece mais ali. Ele atualiza na abertura do VS, no refresh em segundo plano e quando você clica no anel.

Atualizei a versão para 301.0 (AssemblyInfo, manifest, README) e o `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Não fiz commit.

**Para testar:** tem uma instância Exp aberta (PID 46440) que eu não iniciei, então não fechei. Feche ela e aperte F5 de novo (ou rode `./deploy-exp.cmd -run`) para carregar a 301.0. Vale conferir:
- se o "Trocar conta" cai no login com o Google habilitado;
- se o "Conta:" no popup mostra a conta do Claude Code.

  parser and the logout link.

A versão 301.0 está publicada no Marketplace, e o commit `7badb49` foi enviado ao `master`.

- O `publish.cmd` passou nos 1085 testes, recompilou em Release e confirmou o envio para o Marketplace.
- O commit não tem linha de coautoria de IA, conforme a sua regra.

Ainda não testei no VS o "Trocar conta" levando para a tela de login nem o e-mail da conta do Claude Code no popup de uso. O botão do Google foi o que você já confirmou na instância Exp. Quando a 301.0 chegar pelo Marketplace, vale conferir essas duas coisas.

Também atualizei a memória: o problema do botão do Google ficou registrado como resolvido, com o motivo.
